items.title: Section: The Object of Dependent Origination Opens

items.zh: 云何緣性緣起所緣？謂於三世唯行、唯法、唯事、唯因、唯果，墮正道理。謂觀待道理、作用道理、證成道理、法爾道理。唯有諸法能引諸法，無有作者及以受者，是名緣性緣起所緣。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, in the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the second part of the second yogic process … What is the object of dependent origination? It is contemplating, across the three times, only conditioned formations, only phenomena, only events, only causes, and only effects — falling within the correct principles: the principle of dependence, the principle of function, the principle of proof, and the principle of natural law. … Only phenomena drawing forth further phenomena — there is no agent, and no one who experiences the result. This is called the object of dependent origination.

items.zh: 於此所緣作意思惟，癡行增上補特伽羅所有癡行皆得微薄，於諸癡行，心得清淨。是名緣性緣起所緣。

items.title: The Object of the Six Elements Opens

items.zh: 云何界差別所緣？謂六界差別。一、地界，二、水界，三、火界，四、風界，五、空界，六、識界。
items.en: What is the object of the differentiation of elements? It is the differentiation of the six elements: the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, and the consciousness element.

items.title: The Earth Element: Internal and External

items.zh: 云何地界？地界有二。一、內，二、外。內地界者，謂此身中內別堅性，堅鞕所攝、地地所攝，親附、執受。外地界者，謂外堅性，堅鞕所攝、地地所攝，非親附、非執受。又內地界其事云何？謂髮、毛、爪、齒、塵垢、皮、肉、骸骨、筋、脈、肝、膽、心、肺、脾、腎、肚、胃、大腸、小腸、生藏、熟藏，及糞穢等，名內地界。又外地界其事云何？謂瓦、木、塊、礫、樹、石、山、巖，如是等類，名外地界。
items.en: What is the earth element? The earth element is twofold: internal and external. The internal earth element is whatever hard quality within this body belongs to hardness, belongs to earth and to what earth comprises, and is bound to [the body] and appropriated by consciousness. The external earth element is whatever hard quality outside the body belongs to hardness, to earth and to what earth comprises, but is neither bound to [the body] nor appropriated by consciousness. … Hair, body hair, nails, teeth, accumulated grime, skin, flesh, bone, sinew, blood vessels, liver, gallbladder, heart, lungs, spleen, kidneys, stomach lining, stomach, large intestine, small intestine, undigested and digested matter, and excrement — these are the internal earth element. … Tile, wood, clods, gravel, trees, stone, mountains, and cliffs — such things as these are the external earth element.

items.title: The Water Element: Internal and External

items.zh: 云何水界？水界有二。一、內，二、外。內水界者，謂此身中內別濕性，濕潤所攝、水水所攝，親附、執受。其事云何？謂淚、汗、洟、唾、肪、膏、脂、髓、熱痰、膿血、腦、膜、尿等，名內水界。外水界者，謂外濕性，濕潤所攝、水水所攝，非親附，非執受。其事云何？謂井、泉、池、沼、陂、湖、河、海，如是等類，名外水界。
items.en: What is the water element? The water element is twofold: internal and external. The internal water element is whatever moist quality within this body belongs to moisture, belongs to water and to what water comprises, and is bound to [the body] and appropriated by consciousness. … Tears, sweat, mucus, saliva, fat, tallow, marrow, phlegm, pus and blood, brain matter, membrane, and urine — these are the internal water element. The external water element is whatever moist quality outside the body belongs to moisture, to water and to what water comprises, but is neither bound to [the body] nor appropriated by consciousness. … Wells, springs, ponds, marshes, reservoirs, lakes, rivers, and seas — such things as these are the external water element.

items.title: The Fire Element: Internal and External

items.zh: 云何火界？火界有二。一、內，二、外。內火界者，謂此身中內別溫性，溫熱所攝、煖煖所攝，親附、執受。其事云何？謂於身中所有溫煖，能令身熱、等熱、遍熱。由是因緣，所食、所飲、所噉、所甞，易正消變。彼增盛故，墮蒸熱數。如是等類，名內火界。外火界者，謂外溫性，溫熱所攝、煖煖所攝，非親附、非執受。其事云何？謂於人間依鑽燧等、牛糞末等，以求其火。火既生已，能燒牛糞、或草、或薪、或榛、或野、或山、或渚、或村、村分、或城、城分、或國、國分。
items.en: What is the fire element? The fire element is twofold: internal and external. The internal fire element is whatever warm quality within this body belongs to heat, to warmth and to what warmth comprises, bound to [the body] and appropriated by consciousness. … All the warmth within the body, which makes the body hot, hot to the proper degree, or hot throughout. Through this condition, whatever is eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted is readily digested and transformed. … The external fire element is whatever warm quality outside the body belongs to heat, to warmth and to what warmth comprises, but is neither bound to [the body] nor appropriated by consciousness. … In the human world, fire is sought by drilling friction-sticks, by grinding dried dung, and other such means. Once fire has arisen, it can burn dung, grass, firewood … a city or part of a city, a country or part of a country.

items.zh: 或復所餘如是等類，名外火界。

items.title: The Wind Element Opens — Twelve Kinds of Internal Wind

items.zh: 云何風界？風界有二。一、內，二、外。內風界者，謂此身中內別風性，風飄所攝，輕性、動性，親附、執受。其事云何？謂內身中，有上行風、有下行風、有脇臥風、有脊臥風、有腰間風、有臗間風、有小刀風、有大刀風、有針刺風、有畢鉢羅風、有入出息風、有隨支節風。
items.en: What is the wind element? The wind element is twofold: internal and external. The internal wind element is whatever windy quality within this body belongs to motion, being of a light and mobile nature — neither bound to [the body] nor appropriated by consciousness. … Within the body there is upwards-moving wind, downwards-moving wind, side-lying wind, spine-lying wind, waist wind, hip wind, small-blade wind, great-blade wind, needle-piercing wind, mottling wind, in-and-out breath wind, and limb-and-joint wind.

items.title: External Wind, Space, and Consciousness Close the Six Elements

items.zh: 外風界者，謂外風性，風飄所攝，輕性、動性，非親附、非執受。其事云何？謂在身外，有東來風、有西來風、有南來風、有北來風、有有塵風、有無塵風、有狹小風、有廣大風、有毘濕婆風、有吠藍婆風、有風輪風。有時大風卒起積集，折樹、頹牆、崩山、蕩海；既飄鼓已，無所依憑，自然靜息。若諸有情欲求風者，動衣、搖扇、及多羅掌。如是等類，名外風界。云何空界？謂眼、耳、鼻、口、咽喉等所有孔穴。由此吞咽、於此吞咽，既吞咽已，由此孔穴便下漏泄。如是等類，說名空界。云何識界？謂眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意識。又心、意、識三種差別。
items.en: The external wind element is whatever windy quality outside the body belongs to motion, light and mobile in nature, neither bound to [the body] nor appropriated by consciousness. … Outside the body there is wind from the east, west, south, and north; wind carrying dust and wind free of dust; narrow, localised wind and vast, sweeping wind; the wind of primordial world-formation, the whirlwind, and the wind that encircles the world like a wheel. At times a great wind suddenly gathers and rises, snapping trees, toppling walls, collapsing mountains, and stirring seas … What is the space element? It is all the cavities and openings — the eyes, ears, nose, mouth, throat, and so on. Through these one swallows; having swallowed, waste is passed downwards through these same openings. What is the consciousness element? It is the eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness — or, differently divided, mind, mentation, and consciousness.

items.title: Section: The Six Elements Close — Antidote for Pride

items.zh: 若諸慢行補特伽羅，於界差別作意思惟，便於身中離一合想，得不淨想。無復高舉，憍慢微薄，於諸慢行，心得清淨。是名慢行補特伽羅由界差別淨行所緣。
items.en: If a practitioner's dominant affliction is pride, attending to the differentiation of the elements dissolves, within the body, the notion of a single unified mass, giving rise instead to the perception of impurity. No further arrogance arises; conceit thins. This is called the mind of the pride-dominant practitioner being purified through the object of the differentiation of elements.

blocks.text: Fascicle 27 continues the purifying objects: **dependent origination** (for the delusion-type), the **analysis of the elements** (for the pride-type), and **mindfulness of breathing** (for the discursive-type). Then come the skilful objects, the objects for purifying affliction, and the beginning of instruction.

One contemplates "across the three times, only conditioned formations, only phenomena, only events, only causes, and only effects"; "only phenomena drawing forth further phenomena: there is no agent, and no one who experiences the result". Venerable Miào Jìng: "only formations" is just the mind's discrimination.
Earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, each internal and external. Venerable Miào Jìng: formless gods have only space and consciousness.

**Earth** within the body is whatever is hard: hair, nails, teeth, bones, flesh. Venerable Miào Jìng: you don't feel your hair; cutting it doesn't hurt: it is not "appropriated" by consciousness in the same way. **Water**: tears, sweat, saliva, blood, urine. **Fire**: bodily warmth, by which "whatever is eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted is readily digested".

Internal wind: upwards, downwards, in the limbs and joints, the breath. External wind: the winds of the world. **Space**: the body's cavities. **Consciousness**: "eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness; or mind, mentation, and consciousness".

"Attending to the differentiation of the elements dissolves the notion of a single unified mass" in the body. Venerable Miào Jìng: separate parts combine into what seems an indestructible self. "No further arrogance arises; conceit thins."

quiz.q: What does the object of dependent origination contemplate, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the knower from the known?
options: across the three times, only formations, phenomena, events, causes, and effects, in line with correct principle; dependent origination is the object, wisdom the knower
quiz.why: "Contemplating, across the three times, only conditioned formations, only phenomena, only events, only causes, and only effects — falling within the correct principles." Venerable Miào Jìng: dependent origination is the object; your wisdom is what knows it.

quiz.q: "Only phenomena draw forth phenomena; there is no agent and no experiencer." How do the masters explain this?
options: Cháng Bǎi: not created by God, nor by any other person; Miào Jìng: from cause comes effect, from effect arises cause, in a cycle
quiz.why: "Only phenomena drawing forth further phenomena — there is no agent, and no one who experiences the result." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is not created by God, nor is there another person making one's life. Venerable Miào Jìng: from cause comes effect, from effect arises cause — cause to effect, effect to cause.

quiz.q: What are the six elements, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the consciousness element does?
options: earth, water, fire, wind, space, consciousness; without consciousness holding it, the body becomes a corpse unable to cognize
quiz.why: "The earth element, the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, and the consciousness element." Master Cháng Bǎi: if consciousness did not hold the body, it would become a corpse, unable to cognize, like a plant.

quiz.q: The English renders both as relating to consciousness. What examples do the masters use to separate them?
options: both use cutting hair or nails: Miào Jìng says bound but not appropriated; Cháng Bǎi says the painless part is bound, the painful part appropriated
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: you don't feel your hair — cutting it doesn't hurt; cutting your nails doesn't hurt. Master Cháng Bǎi: in cutting nails, the part that doesn't hurt is "bound," the part that hurts is "appropriated."

quiz.q: What does internal fire do, according to the treatise and Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: makes food and drink digest; we say the stomach digests, but here it is fire
quiz.why: "Through this condition, whatever is eaten, drunk, chewed, or tasted is readily digested and transformed." Venerable Miào Jìng: we say the stomach digests; here it says fire digests — with the fire element, everything is digested.

quiz.q: What winds are listed as internal, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say limb-and-joint wind is?
options: upwards, downwards, side-lying, spine-lying … breath, limb-and-joint winds; hands writing and limbs moving are due to wind
quiz.why: "Within the body there is upwards-moving wind, downwards-moving wind … in-and-out breath wind, and limb-and-joint wind." Master Cháng Bǎi: the hand moving to write is limb-and-joint wind; hands and feet move because of wind.

quiz.q: What happens when a pride-dominant practitioner reflects on the elements, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "dissolving the notion of a single mass"?
options: the notion of a unified mass dissolves and the perception of impurity arises; free of self-view, there is no conceit
quiz.why: "If a practitioner's dominant affliction is pride, attending to the differentiation of the elements dissolves, within the body, the notion of a single unified mass, giving rise instead to the perception of impurity." Venerable Miào Jìng: dissolving the unified notion is leaving self-view; without self-view there is no conceit.
